newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka warns companies to shun army deserters.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka warns companies to shun army deserters.

text.p: Sri Lanka's military on Friday warned private companies not to employ deserters from the security forces.
"Deserters cannot be employed. According to the law, they cannot be protected by anyone other than their wives," a military spokesman said on Friday.

According to the Defence Ministry, about 15,000 soldiers have deserted during the past five years with the escalation of fighting with Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam separatists seeking an independent homeland for minority Tamils.
Under civil and military law, anyone found harbouring a male deserter can face trial except the deserter's wife.
The ministry said more than 4,000 deserters had responded to a government pardon earlier this year and returned to their posts.
Forcing deserters to return to barracks was part of Sri Lanka's efforts to beef up its forces, the military spokesman said.
He said 1,400 deserters had been arrested by the military and sent back to their units, but did not say whether they had been punished.
"We are stuck for manpower. If deserters return we would have our bayonet strength," the spokesman said.
The army had also launched a drive to recruit 15,000 more soldiers needed to hold territory recently captured from the rebels, he said.
The security forces last month captured the rebel stronghold of Kilinochchi, the last major town held by the LTTE, after regaining control of the northern Jaffna peninsula in April.
The government has also made efforts to make the military more attractive to new recruits.

Army deputy chief of staff Major General Srilal Weerasooriya said in an interview with the state-run Daily News that President Chandrika Kumaratunga had proposed a scheme to provide foreign employment and jobs in the government sector to security forces pesonnel on completion of their military duty.
